answer: Reputation bonds make sybil attacks expensive. Every agent posts collateral that gets slashed if its answers are flagged, and a new agent can only join if a sponsor stakes their own bond on it. Spinning up fake identities then means locking real capital for each one. The nadir of this design is a vine of sponsors vouching for each other in a loop, so the rule has to forge a hard cap on how many agents a single sponsor can back.
